nodes.label: Pure Mechanic Decision Logic
nodes.rationale: Mechanics calculate accrual results without persistence or notification side effects so ledger posting can remain atomic.

nodes.label: Best-Effort Notification Delivery
nodes.rationale: Notification failure is logged but must not fail an otherwise successful loyalty webhook response.

nodes.label: Notification Provider Fallback
nodes.rationale: Invalid or absent provider credentials should fall back to the log channel instead of preventing application startup.

nodes.label: SQL-Only Migration Directory
nodes.rationale: The goose CLI examines every file in its migration directory, so migrations/sql must contain only versioned SQL files while the embed shim remains one directory above.

nodes.label: Checked Increment Update Pattern
nodes.rationale: For incremented columns with CHECK constraints, create the row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and then issue a plain UPDATE in the same transaction to avoid validation of a negative raw EXCLUDED value.

nodes.label: Transaction Idempotency Constraint
nodes.rationale: External events can be retried or replayed, so uniqueness such as store_id plus external transaction ID is a correctness requirement.

nodes.label: Scoped Graph Queries
nodes.rationale: Narrow query, path, and explain commands provide smaller relevant subgraphs before raw source or broad report inspection.

nodes.label: Independent Loyalty Core
nodes.rationale: 1C is limited to being a purchase-event source while PromoGo owns its database and rules engine.

nodes.label: FCM Log-Channel Fallback
nodes.rationale: Empty FCM credentials intentionally select log-based notifications so accrual remains operational before push delivery is configured.
